title: TypeScript Reference
description: A compact reference of the TypeScript syntax, types, utility types, module forms and compiler options covered in the tutorial, each with a short example and the lesson that explains it.

entries.name: string, number, boolean
entries.summary: The three everyday primitive types. number covers integers and floats alike; inference assigns them from initial values.
entries.syntax: let name: string = "Ada"; let age = 36; let active = true;

entries.name: null and undefined
entries.summary: Separate types under strictNullChecks; a value may hold them only when its type says so with a union.
entries.syntax: let nickname: string | null = null;
notes: Use ?? to supply a default and ?. to access a property of a possibly-missing value.

entries.name: any
entries.summary: Opts a value out of type checking entirely. Avoid it; JSON.parse and untyped packages are the usual sources.
entries.syntax: const raw: any = JSON.parse(text);

entries.name: unknown
entries.summary: The safe top type: accepts every value but must be narrowed before any member is used.
entries.syntax:
const value: unknown = JSON.parse(text);
if (typeof value === "string") { value.toUpperCase(); }

entries.name: never
entries.summary: The type with no values: the return type of a function that always throws, and the result of exhaustive narrowing.
entries.syntax: function fail(msg: string): never { throw new Error(msg); }

entries.name: void
entries.summary: Return type of a function whose result is not meant to be used.
entries.syntax: function log(message: string): void { console.log(message); }

entries.name: Literal types
entries.summary: A single value as a type. const declarations infer literal types; let widens them to the primitive.
entries.syntax: let theme: "light" | "dark" = "light";

entries.name: interface
entries.summary: Names an object shape with required, optional and readonly properties and methods. Interfaces can extend others and merge.
entries.syntax: interface Product { id: number; name: string; tags?: string[]; readonly sku: string; }

entries.name: type
entries.summary: Names any type: primitives, unions, object shapes, tuples or function types. Cannot be reopened or merged.
entries.syntax:
type Id = number | string;
type Handler = (event: string) => void;

entries.name: ?: and readonly
entries.summary: A question mark makes a property optional (its type gains undefined); readonly forbids assignment after creation.
entries.syntax: interface Options { retries?: number; readonly id: string; }

entries.name: Index signature
entries.summary: Describes a dictionary: any key of the given type maps to the value type.
entries.syntax: interface Scores { [player: string]: number; }
notes: Prefer Record<Key, Value> when the set of keys is a known union.

entries.name: Union A | B
entries.summary: A value that is one of several types. Only members shared by every alternative are accessible until narrowed.
entries.syntax: function pad(value: string | number): string

entries.name: Intersection A & B
entries.summary: A type with every property of both operands. Intersecting incompatible types silently produces never.
entries.syntax: type Post = { title: string } & Timestamps;

entries.name: T[] and readonly T[]
entries.summary: An array whose elements all have type T. readonly removes every mutating method.
entries.syntax:
const scores: number[] = [1, 2];
const fixed: readonly string[] = ["a"];

entries.name: Tuple [A, B]
entries.summary: A fixed-length array with a known type per position; positions may be labelled, optional or a rest element.
entries.syntax:
type Point = [x: number, y: number];
function minMax(v: number[]): [min: number, max: number]

entries.name: enum
entries.summary: A set of named constants that compiles to a real object. Numeric members get a reverse mapping; string enums are nominal.
entries.syntax: enum LogLevel { Debug = "debug", Info = "info" }
notes: Not erasable: rejected by erasableSyntaxOnly and by Node's type stripping.
Prefer a literal union or an as const object for most cases.

entries.name: as const
entries.summary: Infers the narrowest, readonly type for a literal, turning arrays into readonly tuples and strings into literal types.
entries.syntax:
const sizes = ["S", "M", "L"] as const;
type Size = (typeof sizes)[number];

entries.name: keyof, typeof and T[K]
entries.summary: keyof T is the union of property names, typeof x is the type of a value, and T[K] reads the type of one property.
entries.syntax:
type Role = User["role"];
type Keys = keyof typeof LOG_LEVELS;

entries.name: satisfies
entries.summary: Checks a value against a type without changing its inferred type, keeping precise literals.
entries.syntax: const config = { port: 3000 } satisfies Config;

entries.name: Function type
entries.summary: The type of a function value: a parameter list and a return type joined by an arrow. Callbacks are contextually typed from it.
entries.syntax: type Formatter = (value: number) => string;

entries.name: Optional, default and rest parameters
entries.summary: A ? or a default value makes a parameter optional; ...rest collects trailing arguments into an array. Optional parameters must come last.
entries.syntax:
function greet(name: string, greeting = "Hello", suffix?: string): string
function sum(...values: number[]): number

entries.name: public, private, protected
entries.summary: Compile-time access control for class members. private is erased; use #name for a field that is private at runtime.
entries.syntax: class Vault { private secret = "x"; #pin = 1234; protected tag = "v"; }

entries.name: Parameter properties
entries.summary: A modifier on a constructor parameter declares the field and assigns it in one step. Not erasable syntax.
entries.syntax: class Counter { constructor(private readonly step: number, public label = "counter") {} }

entries.name: abstract and implements
entries.summary: abstract classes cannot be instantiated and may require methods from subclasses; implements checks a class against an interface.
entries.syntax: abstract class Shape implements HasArea { abstract area(): number; }

entries.name: override
entries.summary: Marks a method that replaces an inherited one, so a misspelled name is an error. noImplicitOverride makes it mandatory.
entries.syntax: class Circle extends Shape { override area(): number { return Math.PI * this.r ** 2; } }

entries.name: Generic function <T>
entries.summary: Declares a type parameter that the compiler infers at each call, preserving the caller's types in the result.
entries.syntax: function first<T>(items: T[]): T | undefined { return items[0]; }

entries.name: T extends Constraint
entries.summary: Limits what a type parameter may be, making the constraint's members available inside the function.
entries.syntax:
function longest<T extends { length: number }>(a: T, b: T): T
function pluck<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K]
notes: Type parameters may have defaults: interface Response<T = unknown>.

entries.name: typeof guard
entries.summary: Narrows a union by primitive type inside the checked branch.
entries.syntax: if (typeof value === "number") { value.toFixed(2); }

entries.name: in and instanceof guards
entries.summary: in narrows by the presence of a property; instanceof narrows to a class and its subclasses.
entries.syntax:
if ("swim" in animal) { animal.swim(); }
if (pet instanceof Dog) { pet.bark(); }

entries.name: Discriminated union
entries.summary: Object types that share a literal-typed property (the discriminant); a switch on it narrows to the matching member.
entries.syntax: type Shape = { kind: "circle"; radius: number } | { kind: "square"; side: number };

entries.name: Exhaustiveness check
entries.summary: Assigning the remaining value to a never variable in the default branch reports any union member without a case.
entries.syntax: default: { const unreachable: never = shape; return unreachable; }

entries.name: Type predicate (x is T)
entries.summary: A function whose return type tells the compiler what a true result proves; works with filter. Simple predicates are inferred since 5.5.
entries.syntax: function isFish(a: Fish | Bird): a is Fish { return "swim" in a; }

entries.name: x! and x as T
entries.summary: The non-null assertion removes null and undefined; a type assertion replaces the type. Neither checks anything at runtime.
entries.syntax:
const el = map.get(key)!;
const user = data as User;
notes: Prefer a real check (if, ??, ?.) or satisfies; use as only when you know more than the compiler can.

entries.name: Partial<T>, Required<T>, Readonly<T>
entries.summary: All properties optional, all required, or all read-only. All three are shallow: nested objects are not affected.
entries.syntax:
type UserUpdate = Partial<User>;
const frozen: Readonly<User> = user;

entries.name: Pick<T, K>, Omit<T, K>
entries.summary: Keep only the listed keys, or everything except them. Compose with Partial for update payloads.
entries.syntax:
type Preview = Pick<User, "id" | "name">;
type NewUser = Omit<User, "id">;

entries.name: Record<K, V>
entries.summary: An object type with exactly the keys K and values V; with a union of keys, every key is required.
entries.syntax: const permissions: Record<Role, string[]> = { admin: ["write"], member: ["read"] };

entries.name: Exclude<U, M>, Extract<U, M>
entries.summary: Filter a union: remove the members assignable to M, or keep only those.
entries.syntax: type Settled = Exclude<Status, "idle" | "loading">;

entries.name: NonNullable<T>
entries.summary: Removes null and undefined from a type.
entries.syntax: type Name = NonNullable<string | null | undefined>; // string

entries.name: ReturnType<F>, Parameters<F>
entries.summary: Extract what a function type returns, or its parameter list as a tuple. Combine with typeof fn.
entries.syntax:
type Created = ReturnType<typeof createUser>;
type Args = Parameters<typeof createUser>;

entries.name: Awaited<T>
entries.summary: The resolved type of a promise, unwrapped recursively; models what await produces.
entries.syntax: type Ids = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof loadIds>>;

entries.name: export and import
entries.summary: Share functions, values, classes and types between files. Under nodenext ES modules, relative paths need the .js extension.
entries.syntax:
export function add(a: number, b: number): number { return a + b; }
import { add } from "./math.js";

entries.name: import type
entries.summary: Imports that exist only for the checker and are erased from the output; required for types under verbatimModuleSyntax.
entries.syntax:
import type { Vector } from "./math.js";
import { add, type Vector } from "./math.js";

entries.name: .d.ts files
entries.summary: Type-only companions to JavaScript: signatures with declare and no bodies. Generated with the declaration option or published as @types packages.
entries.syntax: export declare function distance(a: Point, b: Point): number;

entries.name: @types packages
entries.summary: Community declarations from DefinitelyTyped for JavaScript packages. Fixes TS7016 when the package ships no types.
entries.syntax: npm install --save-dev @types/node

entries.name: declare module
entries.summary: Describes an untyped package yourself in a .d.ts file. The one-line form without a body types every export as any.
entries.syntax: declare module "legacy-slugify" { export default function slugify(input: string): string; }

entries.name: declare global
entries.summary: Adds members to global types such as Window or NodeJS.ProcessEnv from inside a module file.
entries.syntax:
export {};
declare global { namespace NodeJS { interface ProcessEnv { DATABASE_URL: string } } }

entries.name: tsc, --init, --noEmit, --watch
entries.summary: tsc compiles the project in tsconfig.json; --init creates the file, --noEmit only checks, --watch rebuilds on save. tsx runs a file without checking.
entries.syntax:
npx tsc --init
npx tsc --noEmit
npx tsc --watch
npx tsx src/app.ts

entries.name: strict
entries.summary: Enables noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, strictPropertyInitialization, strictFunctionTypes, strictBindCallApply, noImplicitThis, useUnknownInCatchVariables and alwaysStrict.
entries.syntax: "strict": true

entries.name: noUncheckedIndexedAccess
entries.summary: Makes array and index-signature reads T | undefined so out-of-range access must be handled.
entries.syntax: "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true

entries.name: exactOptionalPropertyTypes
entries.summary: An optional property may be absent but not explicitly set to undefined unless its type includes undefined.
entries.syntax: "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true

entries.name: erasableSyntaxOnly
entries.summary: Rejects enums, namespaces with values and parameter properties so the code can run through type stripping (TS 5.8+).
entries.syntax: "erasableSyntaxOnly": true

entries.name: verbatimModuleSyntax
entries.summary: Keeps imports exactly as written; types must be imported with the type keyword (TS1484 otherwise).
entries.syntax: "verbatimModuleSyntax": true

entries.name: module, target, rootDir, outDir
entries.summary: module nodenext follows Node's rules, target sets the emitted JavaScript version, rootDir and outDir map src to dist.
entries.syntax: "module": "nodenext", "target": "es2022", "rootDir": "src", "outDir": "dist"

entries.name: declaration, skipLibCheck, types
entries.summary: declaration emits .d.ts files, skipLibCheck skips checking node_modules declarations, types limits which @types packages load.
entries.syntax: "declaration": true, "skipLibCheck": true, "types": ["node"]
